summary: Migration spec for inventory-service: containerized on Amazon EKS with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL in us-west-2. gaps.handling: Implement parameterised queries for all database access to prevent SQL injection.
Move all hard-coded credentials to AWS Secrets Manager.
Implement proper authentication and authorization for all write endpoints; remove the shared static admin token.
Upgrade Flask to a supported version and use a maintained web framework.
Ensure the database security group allows access only from the application pods.
Enable EBS encryption and disable IMDSv1 for the worker nodes.
Deploy the application with at least 2 replicas across multiple Availability Zones.
Migrate the SQLite database to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
Store the nightly report in an S3 bucket instead of the local filesystem.
Replace the Flask development server with a production-ready server like Gunicorn or Uvicorn.
Implement regular backups of the RDS database.
Use environment variables for configuration instead of hard-coding.
Send logs to CloudWatch or a sidecar container instead of writing to a local file.
Run the scheduled job as a Kubernetes CronJob.
Implement liveness and readiness probes as per the platform standards.

# Migration spec: inventory-service

## Summary
- Replatform legacy inventory and orders application from a single EC2 instance to a containerized microservice on Amazon EKS with Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
- Deploy in us-west-2 with at least 2 replicas across multiple Availability Zones to meet 99.9% availability.
- Target monthly cost is USD 450, using Graviton (arm64) instances for efficiency.
- Implement structured logging, health endpoints, and secure secrets management.

## Key decisions
| Decision | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Platform | eks | G1, TC4 |
| Region | us-west-2 | TC1 |
| Database | Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL, multi-AZ | TC3, G2 |
| CPU architecture | arm64 (Graviton) | TC2, G3 |
| Minimum replicas | 2 | NFR3 |
| Autoscaling metric | CPU | NFR3 |
| Budget | USD 450/month | G3 |
| Logs | JSON to stdout | NFR5 |
| Secrets | AWS Secrets Manager | SEC1 |
| Encryption | At rest and in transit | SEC2 |

## Risks
- Potential cost overrun if traffic grows faster than expected; monitor and adjust scaling.
- Complexity in migrating data from SQLite to RDS; ensure data integrity and minimal downtime.
- Dependence on third-party services (AWS Secrets Manager, RDS) requires proper IAM roles and access control.

<!-- generated: tables rendered from the validated spec -->

## Target specification

| Area | Values |
|---|---|
| Target | eks in us-west-2, Kubernetes 1.33, arm64, IaC terraform, registry ecr |
| Workload | port 8080, probes /healthz and /readyz, replicas 2-6 on cpu 70%, peak 40 rps, p95 300 ms |
| Data | postgres 16 on rds, Multi-AZ yes, migrate from sqlite |
| NFR | SLO 99.9%, RPO 15 min, RTO 60 min, logging json-stdout |
| Security | secrets aws-secrets-manager, encryption at rest yes, private DB yes, non-root yes, read-only root FS yes |
| FinOps | USD 450/month (prod), prefer Graviton yes, growth x3 next year |
